Relative to July, the statement still characterizes current conditions as solid (strong labor market, moderate growth) but adopts a more dovish, risk‑management stance given softer business investment, exports, and below‑target inflation. The SLOOS corroborates emerging headwinds: banks reported tighter standards and other terms for C&I loans and for construction and land development, alongside weaker demand for construction/land development credit; some tightening also showed up in other consumer loans. Offsets include banks’ stated willingness to lend in some consumer categories, mixed/unchanged standards for government loans, and stronger demand for government loans. Taken together, credit supply/demand signals lean tighter at the margin, reinforcing a cautious outlook even as policy actions (rate cut, lower IOER, active OMO/repo) support market functioning. Net tone: mildly positive on current conditions, more negative on the outlook than before; sentiment adjusted down accordingly.
